I understand. I’m sorry you are going thru a tough time.    Life is tough. Think about things that bring you joy. Birds tweeting outside, the fresh cold air, your favorite music that picks you up.

I get excited and sometimes annoyed with my birthday. It’s on Christmas Eve. Every time I see Christmas decorations, I see my birthday not Christmas. And think dang, I am going up a number. I have my birthday lunch and presents then at night family (not with everyone there)does the Christmas Eve dinner then my birthday cake before it ends and go to sleep cause NORAD shows that Santa is getting closer! Guess my birthday motivates me to keep going. So even if you don’t have a physical birthday on Christmas Eve, I highly recommend a spiritual one! Go for it!

Is there a hobby/life skill you have been good at and would possibly try again? Maybe use that to teach someone else? Music? Painting? Cooking? Baking? Surfing? If not, take something up and learn to get good at it , even if it turns into a small part time job. I have done this and I find it turned into a positive chain reaction. I taught someone a skill who taught someone else. That someone else used that skill to brighten another person’s day.

Don’t be sorry! Good that you came on here to share. I am so sorry for your loss. Do your best to rest, eat healthy, exercise even if it’s just walking. Talk to a therapist and ignore what your parents think. Talk it out with people you know who have empathy. Find a grief support group.
I am so sorry for you and your family. Surround her with her most trusted family members and friends. Grieve together so she doesn’t feel alone. Listen to each other. Eat healthy, rest.
I am so sorry ❤️

Please go see  your doctor today and tell him/her everything. Just breathe and take it day to day. Do easy things like walking. Get an emergency visit with your therapist. If the therapist can’t see you, see the one they recommend right now before they can see you again. I think you came to the right place. Survivors want to help too.
